title: Quantum Hopfion rings in the cluster mean-field approximation
authors: Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, Thomas L. Schmidt
abstract: We study the quantum properties of two- and three-dimensional spin textures -- $kπ$-skyrmions and hopfion rings -- within the cluster mean-field approximation (CMFA). By combining the CMFA with a symmetrization procedure, we achieve two key advances: the accurate computation of quantum fluctuations in large spin textures and reliable access to metastable states. These challenges are generally insurmountable using standard methods, which are severely limited by the curse of dimensionality and typically restricted to ground-state properties. Exploiting the cylindrical symmetry of the studied magnetic configurations, we construct one-dimensional chain-like clusters that can be efficiently simulated using the density matrix renormalization group method, while inter-cluster interactions are treated at the mean-field level. The resulting spatial profiles of quantum features such as the local variation of the magnetization length in hopfion rings reveal limitations of the classical micromagnetic model and indicate the necessity of its extension. We demonstrate that the recently proposed regularized micromagnetic equation provides a suitable framework for this purpose.
summary: This work investigates the quantum behavior of magnetic spin textures like skyrmions and hopfion rings using advanced computational techniques. By employing the Cluster Mean-Field Approximation alongside DMRG, the authors overcome dimensionality limitations to accurately calculate quantum fluctuations in these complex topological states. The results highlight where classical micromagnetics breaks down, suggesting necessary extensions to the theoretical framework.
main_problem: The study focuses on accurately computing the quantum properties of topologically non-trivial spin textures, such as skyrmions and hopfion rings.
main_result: The Cluster Mean-Field Approximation (CMFA) successfully computes quantum fluctuations in large spin textures and accesses metastable states, revealing limitations in purely classical micromagnetic models.
method: The authors combine the CMFA with DMRG simulations by exploiting cylindrical symmetry to reduce the problem to an effective 1D chain solvable via Matrix Product States.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a Heisenberg Hamiltonian describing chiral magnets, analyzed in both discrete lattice forms and continuum approximations adapted for cylindrical coordinates.
key_observables: Topological indices (Q, H), local variation of magnetization length |m|, quantum fluctuations, and zero-mode dynamics of the Hopfion ring.
important_parameters: The analysis explores intermediate regimes between purely classical and fully quantum spin textures; key parameters include exchange stiffness (A), DMI constant (D), and anisotropy (K).
main_assumptions: The CMFA treats inter-cluster interactions at a mean-field level, which is an approximation that may underestimate the true quantum fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate DMRG/CMFA results for skyrmion profiles in various geometries and show convergence analysis (energy, variance) of 2D DMRG simulations as bond dimension increases.
paper_structure: The paper moves from defining the continuum micromagnetic Hamiltonian to adapting it into cylindrical coordinates. It then details the application of CMFA combined with DMRG to simulate quantum fluctuations in skyrmion and hopfion ring structures, concluding with comparisons to classical limits.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the heavy reliance on DMRG, cluster mean-field theory, and mapping complex Hamiltonians onto solvable 1D/2D effective models makes this highly relevant for developing numerical techniques applicable to other quantum many-body systems.

(Panel f) Distribution of the magnetization length |m| for the cases when only nearest-neighbor (NN) spin interactions are taken into account (left) and with inclusion of next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) spin interactions (right).

Maxima points are denoted by hollow circles, and the corresponding values for π-, 2π-, and 3π-skyrmions are 0.0028, 0.0085 and 0.083, respectively.

Panel (a): positions of quantum (red) and classical (blue) spins and their couplings for the cluster in the cylinder geometry – a 3D extension of the one provided in Fig. 1(c). Panels (e)-(g): magnetization distribution obtained with the CFMA in the rectangular region bounded by the skyrmion string core spins and dashed lines in panels (b)-(d).
